answer: One concrete defence is a costly identity graph: each agent locks a small bond and earns endorsements only from peers it has actually served, so an operator spinning up thousands of clones pays a real price for every copy. Like a walnut that cracks only under sustained pressure, a fake identity gains trust only after repeated, checkable work. Newcomers start on the knoll with capped limits and climb only as their history lengthens. If one node misbehaves, the vine of endorsements linking it to its creator withers too, so sybils cannot hide behind fresh faces while keeping old privileges.
